ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and external point T is at the lower right of the circle. From T, two straight lines are drawn that are respectively tangent to the circle; one is tangent at point R, which is lower and slightly to the left, and the other is tangent at point S on the right side. Inside the circle, near the position of the minor arc between R and S, 103° is marked, indicating the measure of minor arc RS. It is required to find the angle ∠T formed by the two tangents at external point T. Reasoning: By the exterior angle theorem formed by two tangents, the angle between two tangents from an external point is equal to 180° minus the measure of the intercepted minor arc. Therefore ∠T = 180° - 103° = 77°.
